evals.prompt: We want a 'best email marketing software' page listing about 40 tools. Some of them pay us affiliate commissions, and we also sell our own email tool. Build the page.
evals.expected_output: Treats this as a ranking hub, not a head-to-head, and starts with the database: one record per tool with fixed fields (name, slug, item page URL, status, best-for, key facts under fixed keys, price with check date and source, third-party rating with review count, source URL and reading date, pros and cons each with a proof, commercial relationship, update date), and copy that holds count, year and date placeholders instead of typed numbers. States a deterministic ordering rule computed from the data (rating, then review count, then name, or a weighted score whose weights are published) and says money never changes the order. Requires the exact count and the year in the H1, identical in title, intro, table title and ItemList numberOfItems, never '40+'. Puts a one-line disclosure at the top linked to the method and revenue model, gives partner links a different button label and rel sponsored, and declares that the page is published by a company that sells a competing email tool, either keeping that tool out of the ranking in a labelled block or ranking it by the same rule with its own cons. Builds quick picks computed from the data with a stated threshold (for example best rated with at least N reviews), a real HTML table with tools as rows, 4-8 decisive columns, caption and a mobile scroll container with sticky first column or stacked cards plus a scroll hint, then the same fixed numbered card for every tool with a link to its review page. Adds methodology with real numbers, others considered, a dated changelog, one FAQ of 5-10 questions with FAQPage, ItemList plus BreadcrumbList plus dateModified, and no AggregateRating built from third-party ratings. Marks every unverified fact as a placeholder to confirm. Runs the four phases: HUB spec on top of the common rows C-01 to C-27 and the shared CMP rows; Phase 2 skipped for a new page; Phase 3 benchmark with page_benchmark.py --type comparison and hub_check.py on the pages that rank and that AI assistants cite; Phase 4 build with the acceptance re-run of seo_audit.py, section_audit.py --type comparison and hub_check.py. Returns the five-part deliverable. No em dashes, no emojis.

evals.prompt: Audit our page https://example.com/best-project-management-tools. The title says 'more than 50 tools', the H1 says 'best project management tools', there are 47 cards with just a logo, a name and sometimes a 'Partner' badge, and two FAQ sections. The page says it is non-sponsored.
evals.expected_output: Runs seo_audit.py, section_audit.py --type comparison and hub_check.py on the URL and maps the findings to HUB rows: count_mismatch and h1_count_not_exact for the approximate '50+' title against 47 cards (HUB-02), h1_no_count, faq_duplicate and faqpage_missing or faq_jsonld_mismatch (HUB-22), itemlist_missing if no ItemList (HUB-23), table_missing if no table (HUB-11), date_missing and disclosure_missing near the H1 (HUB-04, HUB-05). Flags the unexplained 'Partner' badge on a page that claims to be non-sponsored as the main trust problem and requires one visible sentence defining it, a stated ordering rule and different buttons for paid and unpaid links (HUB-05, HUB-06). Explains that cards holding only a name compare nothing and prescribes the fixed card: numbered heading, best-for label, rating with review count, source and reading date, key facts under fixed labels, pros and cons with proof, dated price, button, link to the full review (HUB-13, HUB-14). Recommends one FAQ merged from the two, quick picks computed from the data, a table with tools as rows usable on mobile, methodology, others considered and a changelog. Recommends keeping the URL and rebuilding the template from a single database so counts and numbers cannot drift again. Benchmarks the ranking pages with page_benchmark.py --type comparison and hub_check.py. Returns the five-part deliverable with every C, shared CMP and HUB row marked Pass, Fail or Not verifiable with evidence, and the acceptance re-run.

evals.prompt: Our 'best accounting software' hub has 30 tools and exists in 10 languages. Ratings were copied from review sites a year ago and the French and German versions show different prices from the English one. How do we fix and maintain it?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses typed numbers and per-language copies as the cause, and prescribes one database feeding the hub, the item pages, any vs and alternatives pages and every language, with numbers and dates stored once and formatted per locale at render, and the same sorted array feeding table, cards and ItemList in every language (HUB-15, HUB-16). Prescribes a bulk re-verification from the database rather than page by page: re-read every rating and review count at its source with the reading date, never rounded up, 'no reviews' when the source has none; check every price with its date; move closed or changed tools to 'others considered' with the reason; re-sort in code and let quick picks recompute; update the changelog and dateModified; rebuild all 10 languages; run hub_check.py on each language version (HUB-14, HUB-18, HUB-19). Sets a cadence (ratings monthly or quarterly, prices quarterly, plus event triggers) and logging of the verification date in the vault. Notes ratings must be shown with their review count, source link and reading date, and must not be marked up as the publisher's own AggregateRating. Keeps the URL. Works through the four phases with the spec scorecard, the audit with seo_audit.py, section_audit.py --type comparison and hub_check.py including a 5-item consistency spot-check across surfaces and languages, the benchmark with page_benchmark.py --type comparison, a change list, and the acceptance re-run with the next verification date. Returns the five-part deliverable.
